subject: Private deployment — flexible pricing tranches & SLA split proposal
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@lumahealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumahealth.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing conversation

Nikhil — thanks for the overview during Friday's call. A couple of asks from our procurement team as we prepare an internal request: 

1) Can you provide an amortized view of the platform fee if we commit for 24 vs. 36 months? Procurement wants to understand cashflow impact per quarter.
2) We need clarity on SLA tiers for on-prem vs. VPC: specifically, if we pick the "Standard" support tier, what are the SLA credits for downtime that originates in the private-hosted control plane?

Also, can you include any one-time migration credits or professional services allowances you might consider for a first-year deployment?

Appreciate a spreadsheet we can circulate.

— Carlos
Director of IT Procurement
Luma Health
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing conversation

Carlos — thanks for the clear list. I attached a working deck and a detailed pricing_breakdown_v3.xlsx that lays out: 24/36/48 month amortization scenarios, platform fee split options (annual vs. quarterly), and PS/migration credit proposals. High level: 

- 24-month commit: platform fee amortized quarterly = $Xk (spread evenly).
- 36-month commit: ~12% lower effective platform fee per month due to multi-year discount (details in the sheet).
- One-time migration credit: we can offer up to $45k in PS credits applied against first invoice for a 24-month commit, or $70k for 36 months.

Key negotiation levers I expect they'll push on: initial platform fee cap, support on-call hours, and response SLAs for private control-plane incidents. Laura — can you confirm the exact SLA credit table we should share for "Standard" vs "Priority" support when the control plane is customer-hosted? I want to include the fallback behavior if we need to spin up a hosted variant during an outage.

Carlos — is your procurement team able to accept a tranche billing model (Platform fee billed in three equal annual tranches for a 36-month term) or do they need strictly quarterly invoices? If tranches are acceptable we can stretch the CapEx vs OpEx conversation more favorably.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_breakdown_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), Luma_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW draft)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing conversation

Hey team — quick note on SLAs and credits: 

- Standard Support (included): 24x5 monitoring, 4-hour P1 response, no guaranteed remediation window for private control plane incidents; credit = 5% of monthly platform fee for P1 SLA breach.
- Priority Support (add-on): 24x7 with 2-hour P1 response and 8-hour remediation target; credit = 15% of monthly platform fee for P1 breach.
- Hosted fallback policy: if the customer's private control plane is unreachable and Redwood's hosted fallback is used to restore service, the fallback hours are billable at a reduced rate and we provide a one-time migration credit to offset the temporary integration work.

We can produce a formal SLA addendum for inclusion in the SOW. Nikhil — suggest we present two priced options: (A) 24-month term with $45k PS credit and Standard support; (B) 36-month term with $70k PS credit and Priority support at a 12% discount on platform fee. That keeps it simple for procurement to compare.

-Laura
Head of Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@lumahealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumahealth.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing conversation

Nikhil/Laura — thanks, that helps. A few clarifying items from procurement: 

1) Tranche billing: Luma can accept annual tranche billing but needs an amortization schedule that maps to our internal capital plan — please include the CAPEX impact per fiscal year (FY27 / FY28).
2) Can the PS credit be allocated as a dollar credit on the invoice rather than a line-item service? Procurement prefers credits applied to the invoice total.
3) Regarding the hosted fallback: we want guaranteed notice windows and a transparent change-log if Redwood initiates a fallback that alters data flow. Can you add a paragraph to the SOW clarifying governance and notification steps?

If you send an updated SOW and the amortization table I will take this to our CFO for a cost review. Expect a follow-up by the end of next week.

— Carlos
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing conversation

Carlos — attached an updated SOW (Luma_SOW_v2.pdf) and a revised pricing_breakdown_v3.xlsx with: 

- CAPEX mapping for FY27 / FY28 under both 24- and 36-month tranche schedules.
- PS credit presented as invoice-level credit rows (we will apply credit to first invoice).
- Added SOW paragraph 6.3: "Hosted fallback governance" that commits Redwood to 48-hour notification where possible, real-time post-fallback changelog, and a joint incident review within five business days.

Next steps suggested:
- If tranche billing passes CFO review, confirm which term (24 vs 36).
- If they pick 36, we include Priority support and the 12% effective platform fee discount; otherwise Standard support applies.

Marissa — can you draft a one-page summary we can hand to procurement that lists the two options and the final takeaways (credits, invoice application, fallback governance) so Carlos can circulate?

Carlos — happy to jump on a quick call if that speeds sign-off.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_breakdown_v3.xlsx (updated), Luma_SOW_v2.pdf (updated)
